title: Unlimited Indemnification and Consequential Damages
content: Clauses making freelancer indemnify client for all claims without any monetary cap or including indirect, incidental, and consequential damages. Standard terms: Mutual liability cap strictly limited to total fees paid or payable by client under the specific statement of work in the preceding 6 or 12 months, with mutual waiver of consequential damages.
source: Standard AIGA & Freelancers Union Contract Clause § 8 (Limitation of Liability)

title: Immediate Work-For-Hire Assignment Without Full Payment
content: Clauses assigning all intellectual property rights to the client immediately upon creation or before complete payment has cleared. Standard terms: Assignment of intellectual property rights, work product, and copyright is strictly conditioned upon receipt of full and final payment of all outstanding invoices.
source: Graphic Artists Guild Handbook & Model Consulting Agreements

title: Extreme Payment Terms (Net-60 / Net-90) & No Late Interest
content: Clauses requiring freelancer to accept Net-60 or Net-90 payment terms or forbidding late payment interest. Standard terms: Invoices payable Net-15 or Net-30 from date of invoice. Late payments accrue interest at 1.5% per month (or statutory maximum) plus reimbursement of reasonable collection costs.
source: Freelance Isn't Free Act (FIFA) & European Late Payment Directive

title: Client Exclusivity and Overly Broad Non-Compete
content: Clauses restricting a freelance contractor from taking on other clients in the same industry during or after the engagement. Standard terms: Independent contractor retains full liberty to perform similar services for other clients, provided client confidential information is not breached.
source: IRS Independent Contractor Common Law Rules & Restatement (Second) of Contracts

title: Unilateral Termination Without Payment for In-Progress Work
content: Clauses permitting client to cancel the contract immediately at convenience without paying for work performed or committed resources. Standard terms: Either party may terminate with 14 days written notice; upon termination, client must pay for all completed work and pro-rata for in-progress work plus non-refundable expenses.
